approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using accepted task-local scores. It keeps a bounded score-ranked breeding population, draws parents from high-scoring rank bands, and produces either connected-fragment crossovers with optional finishing mutation or ordinary mutation walks. Ordinary walks usually make one edit call and sometimes two or three; obstruction can force longer walks. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. At each suggestion the Parent fits its count-fingerprint Gaussian process to the complete accepted archive, generates a fresh surplus pool containing only final products, and uses correlated posterior draws to choose the announced evaluation batch. Real accepted scores then update both breeding survivors and the next model fit. The model is already fitted when a mutation walk starts, but does not guide its intermediate steps.
approach.novelty: Add two-arm posterior-mean guidance to optional ordinary continuation. After the unchanged first mutation, each requested second or third step at the ordinary saturation floor tries two fresh mutations from the same current intermediate and continues with the higher predicted raw score. Only the chosen path's final product can enter the original pool. Earlier siblings removed continuation, admitted intermediate products into finite pool slots, or changed predictive fitting and final allocation. This variant preserves the continuation schedule, independent final-product slots and correlated final selector while changing one decision inside the walk. It tests whether an existing useful predictor can guide the next graph step; a predicted arm advantage is evidence of that decision, not measured score improvement.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-62daf219c70a fits its accepted-label GP before graph generation but follows a single unguided mutation at each continuation position, postponing predictive competition until completed products reach the final pool. Its actual summaries and logs contain a complete mean 0.5956696497334577 with seed population SD 0.02659287062806747. The indexed chronological audit records 41,627 ordinary attempts, 7,499 multi-call paths and 8,737 realized optional continuation calls; 322 multi-call final products were accepted, with 46 parent beats and 20 incumbent gains. Across all 4,350 accepted offspring there were only 629 parent beats, and mean child-minus-best-parent was -0.08520023139935991. These measurements expose an unused guidance interface, not proof that its absence causes the endpoint limit. On this same Parent/profile, n-dbee08307e86 removes only floor-one continuation and loses 0.02686763734135833, whereas n-79bc7a1dd0dc harvests prefixes into the fixed pool and loses 0.040929502794467686 while reducing independent attempts from 75,961 to 67,373. The positive retained-selector control n-01b48dd09404 supports preserving final predictive allocation, and n-5a357a2ac96f supports retaining separate crossover finishing. Calibration n-38bcd7569cce and incumbent-referenced batch utility n-8a62df15e51f changed model preferences or diagnostics but lost endpoints. The proposed limitation is specifically the unguided optional step, with its causal value still to be tested.
hypothesis: Modify optional ordinary second/third mutation continuation at saturation floor one by drawing exactly two fresh arms from the same current intermediate and continuing with the valid arm of greatest raw-score posterior mean from the existing suggestion-entry accepted-label count GP, with first-arm exact ties and bounded inherited fallbacks, while retaining the full final-product pool and correlated final selector.

finding_summary.headline: Two-arm choices reached evaluation and later breeding, but mean Top-1 fell by 0.048083
finding_summary.insights: This result rules out lack of execution, absent evaluated delivery, lost feedback, zero cohort-level recursion and reduced final-pool capacity as explanations for the failure of this fixed rule. The model successfully imposed its preferences without producing better search. Across all accepted offspring, mean raw score fell from 0.385256 to 0.326704 while mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.395280. Parent-beating counts rose from 629 to 690 and incumbent-update counts from 258 to 261, yet total incumbent increments fell from 5.807663 to 5.086425. More local wins therefore coexist with weaker sources and less endpoint progress. Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.012718 to 0.007832, but the labels being predicted changed and recorded 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 76.28% to 74.60%; this does not establish better transferable calibration. Chemistry inspection likewise finds both recognizable aromatic amides and amines and persistent questionable bond environments, ring geometries and unresolved stereochemistry. The largest deficits include failure to reproduce a compact high-scoring heterocyclic combination, but neither missing rings/amines nor a specific chemical mediator is established. Most unchosen arms remain unscored, and no alternate continuation future was executed. The evidence supports a negative total contribution of this exact fixed guidance rule under these conditions; it leaves the separate roles of local prediction preferences, extra random draws and later adaptive history unresolved, and does not reverse the value of ordinary continuation itself.
finding_summary.results: The continuation rule executed 8,640 two-arm decisions. Independently reconstructed predictions confirm 4,266 strict choices of a different second-arm identity; 44 exact ties chose the first arm. Those changed paths delivered 237 distinct evaluated finals. All 230 with another suggestion remaining entered the next model fit, and 120 later served as breeding parents. The audit also retains 110 nonterminal finals with no later use and seven terminal births; one task/seed had six affected accepted finals and no later breeding. Final proposal capacity stayed at 160 products per suggestion. Nevertheless, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.547587, a paired change of -0.048083 against the required +0.002. All three seed macros and all five task means decreased; four of the 15 individual task/seed cells improved. Macro population SD declined from 0.026593 to 0.017941, but the gain criterion failed.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides and aryl amines coexist with enlarged heterocycles, reactive bonds and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-87c89dda7e3b produces substituted indole amides, azaaromatic methylamines, compressed ring systems, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione assemblies, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, medium-ring lactams and fluorinated imino/dione heterocycles. Ordinary medicinal-chemistry groups are present, but many outputs also contain unusual heteroatom bonds, large repeated assemblies or unresolved ring geometry. Some leaders are appreciably more conventional than their close high-scoring relatives; neither universal implausibility nor a general absence of rings, amines or heterocycles fits the evidence. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with recurring leading families within individual streams. The weak drug-likeness judgement concerns the mixed output and its liabilities, not a claim that every compound is unsuitable. No synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity has been established by this inspection. The digest was read before all 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory files. All paths exist; all 9,000 records were read, covering every task and Search Seed 0, 1 and 2. Each task has 900 Child records, including 870 evaluated optimizer proposals. There are no tasks without trajectories. The immutable comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile mismatch. This is therefore a complete descriptive chemistry comparison with n-62daf219c70a, not an absent or partial Parent comparison. The profile is the supplied Research in Depth profile, 300 observations per task and feedback batch size 10, with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. The Parent source of record is runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-62daf219c70a/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories; its full Molecular report and the original n-c55c3d520a2c gap report were read through the supplied evidence index. Current gaps retain that historical provenance while describing changed current molecules. In fixed task order, digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9655, 0.9747, 0.9862, 0.9839 and 0.9517; aromatic-atom-string incidences are 0.9644, 0.9736, 0.9839, 0.9747 and 0.9506. These are molecule-level SMILES-text incidences, not aromatic atom fractions or ring counts. Every task has charged-string and stereocentre-string incidence 0.0. Neutral strings nevertheless contain readily recognizable ionizable amines. Independent RDKit readings of evaluated optimizer molecules give median heavy-atom counts 25, 43, 33, 32 and 27; no optimizer row failed parsing. Parsing does not certify chemical feasibility. All counts and molecule descriptors below derive from these supplied trajectories; the audit and annotated row provenance are in .slots/round-0024-slot-1/molecular_chemistry_audit_slot1.json and molecular_annotated_trajectories_slot1.jsonl. Scores are the recorded labels, never recomputed. Last emissions are distinguished from retained best molecules. Unchosen continuation arms have no labels here and receive no chemical outcome credit. Changed chemical families, alert counts or high-score associations do not identify activation, component contribution, mediation, or the cause of any endpoint difference.

per_task.generated_character: Evaluated proposals have median 25 heavy atoms, range 1-41, and predominantly aromatic ring systems. Seed 2 reaches a 24-heavy-atom ethynyl/dimethyl/methoxy indole carboxamide attached to pyridine: a recognizable three-ring heteroaryl amide without a halogen or sulfur triple bond. Seed 0 instead reaches a 25-heavy-atom dimethoxy azaaromatic bicyclic region joined through methylene and an N-chloro or N-bromo aniline nitrogen to a fluorophenyl ring; this leading family has no carbonyl. Seed 1 reaches a 24-heavy-atom oxygenated, tightly connected ring framework carrying an imine, a ketone and an amino/pyridyl side chain; RDKit perceives four-membered closures and an unassigned centre. The stream can therefore make conventional aromatic amides, but it also explores strained connectivities and carbon-sulfur triple-bond strings. Such sulfur bonds occur in 95 of 870 Child optimizer rows versus none of the matched Parent rows for this task. N-halogen bonds occur in 314 Child rows versus 445 Parent rows, so one liability declines while another appears.
liabilities: N-Cl and N-Br substitution occurs on amine or amide nitrogen in strong examples; the carbon-sulfur triple-bond strings are particularly unusual synthetic targets.
Dense small-ring connectivity in seed 1 and its unspecified stereochemical centre leave geometry and molecular identity unresolved.
Tiny floor-scoring molecules are still evaluated late, including the seed-0 NCl and seed-1 oxetane at evaluation 286.
missing_features: Consistent conventional bond environments around the favorable compact aromatic/polar arrangement are missing across the emitted set, although the leading seed-2 indole amide is an explicit counterexample to universal chemical implausibility.
Independent feasible replacements for the compressed seed-1 topology are not demonstrated at its leading score; a ring-rich string alone does not establish a geometrically accessible scaffold.

The observed scores do not identify a unique absent target pharmacophore. Amide, carbonyl-free azaaromatic and constrained families all score above the initial best, so no single functional group can be prescribed from this panel.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The conventional ethynyl indole amide at seed 2 evaluation 256 reaches 0.447213595499958; the sulfur-triple-bond relative at evaluation 208 scores 0.4357560621547693. These differ at several substituents and do not isolate a sulfur-bond effect, but the best observed score plainly does not require that unusual bond. The seed-0 N-Cl and N-Br analogues at evaluations 241 and 282 tie at 0.436818201428663, while the compressed seed-1 framework reaches 0.40282869817021466. NCl, methane and oxetane each score 0.0 in the cited rows: isolated groups or ring presence alone do not reproduce the reward. The visible association is with a compact combined aromatic/polar arrangement; an amide is useful in one family but absent from another leader. Matched Parent best scores in seed order are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596, 0.438972502037081; Child values are 0.436818201428663, 0.40282869817021466, 0.447213595499958. Thus the changed families include both favorable and adverse seed comparisons. Parent leaders also retain N-halogen or cumulene liabilities, so those comparisons are not a chemical-quality standard.

per_task.generated_character: This is the most enlarged output family: median 43 heavy atoms and maximum 120, compared with 33 and 100 in the Parent. Digest mean SMILES length is 85.6. The seed-2 leader has 50 heavy atoms and joins nitrogen heteroaromatics to a carbonyl/thione-containing aromatic-labelled nine-membered ring, with an enyne/diyne appendage, chloromethyl and bromoethyl-ester groups. A near-leading 37-heavy-atom relative instead has a conventional fused five/six-membered heterocyclic region. Seed 0 favors a 37-heavy-atom linked aminopyridine/azole assembly with N-acyl, vinyl, ketone and aldehyde functionality. Seed 1 reaches a 62-heavy-atom repeated fused nitrogen-dione assembly; nearby examples use peroxide linkages and N-halogen bonds. These are rich ring graphs, but their repeated units, numerous heteroatoms and reactive attachments make straightforward synthesis and ordinary drug-like size doubtful.
liabilities: Oversized repeated heterocycles carry many carbonyl and heteroatom groups while giving only modest changes within the observed score band.
Strong examples include peroxides, N-halogen bonds, haloalkyl esters, chloromethyl groups and cumulene chains; these raise environment-specific reactivity and synthesis concerns.

Aromatic notation on a nine-membered heterocycle does not establish an accessible planar aromatic state. The near-tied smaller fused-ring relative shows that this unusual topology is not universally required.
missing_features: Compact alternatives retaining the favorable linked nitrogen/carbonyl/thione organization are not consistently delivered at the stronger Parent score. Compactness is already possible in the Child and is not itself a demonstrated causal remedy.
Conventional, synthetically credible substitutes for the repeated peroxide/N-halogen assemblies and haloalkynyl appendages are not established at their recorded scores.

The larger aromatic-labelled ring lacks demonstrated conformational and tautomeric identity; no exact missing objective-specific arrangement can be inferred solely from the Parent/Child family difference.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. Child seed leaders score 0.6010870669511328, 0.5968277867192773, 0.6097957431147641; matched Parent leaders score 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055, 0.6178024026512013. The Parent seed-0 leader is a compact 30-heavy-atom linked fused nitrogen/carbonyl/thione system, although it too contains reactive oxygen/halogen and ether substituents. The Child does not reproduce that high-scoring combination in its leading output. Within Child seed 2, the 50-heavy-atom evaluation-289 leader scores 0.6097957431147641 and the smaller 37-heavy-atom evaluation-296 relative scores 0.6095356709459028. Several larger variants, including differing cumulated side chains at evaluations 261 and 299, share 0.6077788191190253. The 120-heavy-atom assembly at evaluation 57 scores only 0.565359477124183. Size, repeated rings and extra unsaturation therefore do not uniformly buy reward. Hydrazine and an isolated haloalkyne sit at 0.5; that floor is not evidence of useful chemistry. The observed gradient concerns particular combined heterocyclic arrangements, with considerable peripheral indifference, rather than a general demand for more rings or atoms.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have median 33 heavy atoms, range 1-107. The seed-0 leader is a relatively conventional 25-heavy-atom molecule with two alkyl-linked phenyl rings, two primary amines, two phenols and carbon-bound fluorine. Seed 2 builds fluorinated/chlorinated aryl groups and a dimethylaminophenol around saturated five-membered diamine or piperazine rings, connected through flexible carbon or thioether-containing chains. The 30-heavy-atom seed-2 leader has a five-membered diamine. Seed 1 instead retains an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre written with oxo, hydroxyl, aryl and nitrogen bonds, along with a four-membered nitrogen ring, pyrrolidine, chloromethyl and fluorinated aryl groups; its leader has 33 heavy atoms. Accessible aliphatic amines and saturated nitrogen rings are plainly present. Conventional examples have recognizable synthetic handles, while the sulfur-rich and small-ring variants are less convincing. RDKit finds unassigned potential atom centres in 848 of 870 optimizer rows, with none assigned.
liabilities: The seed-1 hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur environment, small nitrogen rings and chloromethyl group warrant chemical scrutiny; representability is not proof of an ordinary stable sulfur functional group.
Flexible multiply aminated chains, phenols, thioethers and occasional N-O or O-Cl substituents leave stability, oxidation and solution-state behaviour unresolved.
The neutral SMILES omit stereochemical assignments even where the parsed structures contain potential centres; neutral notation does not mean the amines are nonionizable.
missing_features: The missing capability is reliable presentation of the already present aromatic/available-amine organization in conventional, resolved structures; neither basic nitrogen nor saturated nitrogen rings are absent.

Specified stereochemical identity is absent for the branched chains, fluorinated centres and substituted nitrogen rings. Actual protonation and conformational preferences are unmeasured by this audit.

No observed matched molecular comparison identifies a unique additional pharmacophore needed to recover the Parent values. The seed-0 conventional amines are a counterexample to a claim that all strong outputs require unusual sulfur or nitrogen-halogen chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best shown scores 0.01904115112334333. N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine/amide fragments at seed 2 evaluations 18 and 17 score 0.00016650955053713697 and 0.0002562175393167918. The two-primary-amine/diaryl phenol leader reaches 0.9939842754428707. Its O-amino relative at seed 0 evaluation 271 scores 0.9898084892495691, so the extra N-O bond is not needed for the stronger observed result. The five-membered diamine leader reaches 0.977819851459075 and a piperazine relative reaches 0.9725770376635565. These examples associate accessible aliphatic nitrogen plus aromatic surfaces with high labels; they do not isolate a pKa, amine count or specific binding interaction. The 107-heavy-atom early assembly scores 0.02885837683273389, showing that aromatic bulk alone is insufficient. Matched Parent best values are 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906, 0.9999934235240012, versus Child values 0.9939842754428707, 0.9070585904439784, 0.977819851459075. The lower seed-1 Child stream retains the unusual sulfur/small-ring family, but that association does not establish that this chemistry caused its deficit. These are oracle labels, not measured affinity, selectivity or verified docking geometry.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have median 32 heavy atoms, range 1-62, with substantially less halogen incidence than the other streams: the digest halogen-string rate is 0.177. The seed-1 leader has 33 heavy atoms and links a substituted quinoline through methylene ether to an aryl-fused 11-membered lactam ring containing additional N-methyl amines. Seed 0 has 34-heavy-atom diaryl ether/amine frameworks joined through an exocyclic alkene to a bridged nitrogen dicarbonyl system with a four-membered ring. Seed 2 has a 30-heavy-atom quinoline linked to nitrogen-containing seven-membered ring paths and two carbonyl groups. These combine recognizable ethers, amines, lactams and aromatic surfaces, but the bridges and medium rings create substantial route and conformational questions. They are not ring-deficient or heteroatom-deficient fragments. The Parent shows related quinoline/dicarbonyl and bridged diaryl families, rather than an entirely separate chemical regime.
liabilities: Dense four-membered/medium-ring junctions and exocyclic unsaturation complicate geometric feasibility and synthesis even when all atoms have accepted valence.
The macrocyclic-lactam family is not intrinsically impossible, but no route or populated conformation is demonstrated; larger ring count is not evidence of richer useful chemistry.
Peripheral N-O insertion and further elaboration can reduce the score while retaining the same difficult framework; neither complexity nor heteroatom count is monotonically rewarded.
missing_features: Chemically independent, geometrically characterized alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic/amine/carbonyl relationship are not established; current leaders repeatedly retain medium-ring or bridged connectivity.

Explicit stereochemical identity is missing in the bridged and saturated examples, although the leading seed-1 macrocyclic graph has no RDKit-enumerated unassigned atom centre and still has unmeasured conformational preferences.
No unique absent target motif is resolved by the small differences among the leading families. Conventional nitrogen, oxygen, carbonyl and aromatic functions already occur together.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, while acetylene and peroxide score 0.0. Seed-1 evaluation 264, the quinoline/macrocyclic-lactam leader, scores 0.22653939982357355; its methyl-for-ethyl relative at evaluation 194 scores 0.2240284446102978. Enlarging the lactam closure with an N-O connection at evaluation 294 gives 0.22271156434457534. The seed-0 evaluation-254 and evaluation-288 molecules tie at 0.22427840319352513 despite a nitrogen-to-carbon ring-site difference. This supports tolerance of more than one local nitrogen arrangement, not an exact missing heteroatom prescription. A 62-heavy-atom repeated early assembly scores 0.1273277339340891, below the initial best. The combined aromatic/amine/carbonyl organization matters more visibly than simply increasing size or ring count. Child seed leaders are 0.22427840319352513, 0.22653939982357355, 0.21763406411564537; matched Parent leaders are 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601, 0.22600312875247064. The seed-1 improvement and seed-0/seed-2 decreases coexist. The final seed-2 emission scores 0.2044644469050835, below its retained 0.21763406411564537 leader; it is not the endpoint incumbent.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have median 27 heavy atoms, range 1-61. The seed-0 leader is a 27-heavy-atom fused five/six-membered nitrogen dione carrying an imidoyl-fluoride group, N-alkoxymethyl substitution and a fluorinated alkenyl chain. Its fluorines are carbon-bound, not N-F. Seed 1 instead joins a hydroxypyridine to an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen-dione ring with N-fluorine, alkyl and haloalkyl groups; a close high-scoring relative replaces N-F with N-fluoroalkyl substitution. Seed 2 reaches a 28-heavy-atom framework with two perceived nine-membered aromatic rings, carbonyls and a fluorinated thiol-containing ketone side chain. The smaller fused core is more conventional than the large aromatic-labelled rings, but the imidoyl fluoride, unsaturated substitution and solution-state identities still require scrutiny. Child N-halogen incidence is 251 of 870 optimizer rows versus 476 in the Parent; digest cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is only 0.0011. Those reductions do not remove the large-ring or other local bonding concerns.
liabilities: The imidoyl-fluoride substituent is an unusual electrophilic motif, while some other leaders retain N-F bonds or haloalkyl groups. Carbon-bound fluorination itself is not a blanket liability.
Two nine-membered rings labelled aromatic, or a single expanded nitrogen-dione ring, require geometry and tautomer checks beyond SMILES acceptance.
Tiny fluorine-containing emissions remain late in the stream, while early repeated assemblies are extremely low scoring; both loss of context and excessive elaboration are visible.
missing_features: A conventional, geometrically credible alternative to the large aromatic-labelled rings is not demonstrated at those seeds' leading scores. The seed-0 fused core shows that large rings and N-F bonds are not universal requirements.

The favorable compact fluorinated/polar organization is not consistently expressed with ordinary stable functional groups; imidoyl fluoride, N-F and unusual ring representations remain among strong outputs.

Stereochemical identity of the fluorinated saturated seed-2 chain and the tautomeric, imine/alkene and conformational identities of the heterocycles are unresolved. The trajectory does not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. A 61-heavy-atom repeated assembly scores 2.172448175403814e-55, and isolated F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. Compact fluorinated/polar context therefore distinguishes the stronger examples from both oversized assemblies and isolated fluorine. Seed-0 evaluations 249 and 295 tie at 0.5982938487029426 despite redistributing chain length between substituents. Adding ring fluorine to the evaluation-249 framework gives 0.5747204524361843 at evaluation 185; shortening its ether chain gives 0.5538371951991591 at evaluation 262. More fluorine is therefore not a universal rule. Seed 1 reaches 0.5029757502352215, with a no-N-F relative at 0.499543770076088; removing terminal chlorine from the leading framework gives 0.43987096141929904. Seed 2 reaches 0.47065134047819507, whereas its more fluorinated final emission scores 0.34837829103775814. The exact group context matters, but none of these labels establishes feasibility. Matched Parent seed leaders score 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067, 0.7208853668418119, versus Child values 0.5982938487029426, 0.5029757502352215, 0.47065134047819507. The Parent seed-2 leader contains a small cyclic cumulene of doubtful geometry. Its stronger label does not make that motif a required or chemically credible answer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Strong emitted examples include N-halogen bonds, peroxide links, an imidoyl fluoride, an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur environment and carbon-sulfur triple-bond strings. One current aromatic-amide stream has 95 sulfur-triple-bond outputs versus none in its matched Parent stream, yet its best molecule contains an ordinary terminal alkyne instead. Conventional indole amides, primary arylalkyl amines and saturated diamine rings are counterexamples to a universal inability to generate plausible groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while retaining otherwise useful aromatic and polar structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need awareness of the bonding environment and the ability to offer conventional alternatives while preserving combinations supported by local accepted feedback. Ordinary carbon-bound halogens and useful amines must remain distinguishable from unusual heteroatom bonds. These observations justify a chemical capability gap, not a universal filter, a guaranteed score gain, or attribution to the current continuation decision.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Current leading families include compressed four-membered closures, medium-ring bridged carbonyl systems and aromatic-labelled nine-membered heterocycles. Historical Parent cyclic-cumulene concerns remain source-specific; the current best fused fluorinated dione does not require a cyclic cumulene. Conventional fused indoles and saturated diamines are present, and a smaller fused heterocycle nearly ties a larger expanded-ring relative. Ring richness is therefore real, but reliable geometric credibility is not established.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish a valid ring graph from a credible ring geometry and unsaturation pattern.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction and scaffold changes need ring-size, bridge-connectivity and unsaturation awareness, together with feasible alternative connectivities that retain learned functional relationships. Aromatic labels and ring counts cannot supply that information. This is not a ban on small or medium rings, nor evidence that geometric scrutiny would itself improve the recorded objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Every digest task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0. Parsed current arylalkyl amines, substituted diamines, bridged carbonyl frameworks and fluorinated chains contain unassigned potential atom centres; one emitted aryl-amine stream has such centres in 848 of 870 optimizer rows, with none assigned. Some compact aromatic leaders have no enumerated atom centre, so this gap applies when a structure actually requires specification. Charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but recognizable ionizable amines are already present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not resolve stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemistry when relevant, while keeping achiral and configurationally unstable cases distinct. Protonation, tautomerism and conformational identity are separate questions. This evidence establishes unspecified chemical identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or a missing basic-amine capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Current evaluated streams contain tiny floor-scoring fragments late in search and repeated heterocyclic assemblies up to 120 heavy atoms. A 37-heavy-atom heterocycle nearly ties a 50-heavy-atom relative; other enlarged repeated assemblies score below their initial useful context. Conversely, compact indole amides and arylalkyl amines score strongly, showing that simplification and useful small structures are possible. Neither smallness nor bigness is intrinsically rewarded across these records.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain useful molecular context while controlling fragmentation and redundant elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Proposals need feedback-informed ways to preserve functional-group relationships while simplifying, replacing or expanding dispensable portions. The capability gap is consistent context control, not an inability to add atoms or form rings. A fixed minimum size, automatic growth preference or universal fragmentation prohibition does not follow, and the observed molecule associations do not identify which retained component produced them.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Strong excerpts repeatedly alter short chains, halogen placement, ether length, local nitrogen sites or ring segments within retained aromatic-amide, linked heterocycle, aryl-amine, macrocyclic-lactam and fluorinated-dione families. The Child and Parent do show different families across seeds, including conventional counterexamples, so global structural collapse is not supported. Many distinct SMILES and high ring-string incidence do not establish broad useful feasible scaffold coverage within an individual adaptive stream.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently furnish chemically independent plausible alternatives to each seed's leading family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scaffold-level proposals need to reorganize locally supported functional relationships into chemically independent, credible connectivities. Actual accepted labels and chemical plausibility must distinguish useful alternatives from merely distinct graph strings. This conditional coverage gap neither identifies a target-specific scaffold nor proves that more diversity, or any particular search component, would improve the endpoint.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
